summary: All finite evidence retains the single weaving sense. Objects can be yarn/material or cloth/product, with silk, rugs and transport cloths named explicitly; the etymological 'spin' gloss is not projected onto these verses.

Preterit zqərre/zqəlli/zqəllan and Infectum gzəqann-/zoqall- show different assimilations of root-final r. Retain spellings and separate their boxes rather than infer the form from the edition's tense.
zuqriwo/zuqrinawo and zoqarwo support a new Infectum-wa box across JTM and Prym–Socin; habitual labour and simultaneous background weaving both occur.
The Imperativ zqallanyo encodes the assisted beneficiaries and woven theme separately; no new lexical sense follows from the clitics.

zaqoro/zaqore are well-attested profession/agent nouns, including complements naming woven goods. Their noun status is clear; assignment to the glossary's Part act. needs an explicit editorial convention. They are not published as a new box here.

JTM3.4/7 includes two zuqriwo tokens but supplies only one indexed record for that form, plus a separate zuqrinawo record. Decisions cover exactly the supplied 33 records; no invented occurrence line is added.
Existing aliases prs225/5 = supplied PrS77/23 and existing 94/5, 115/5 prevent several reader additions from being new examples.
Does the glossary intentionally include occupational qaṭṭāl nouns such as zaqoro under Part act.? If so, establish that convention before adding this new box.
What creatures are zaqore in PrS61/64? The edition's Mücken? is uncertain; do not identify a species from translation alone.
Verify the reader's unindexed repeated zuqriwo at JTM3.4/7 if token-complete corpus accounting is required.
At 94/5 the inherited English describes patches while the supplied German describes rags prepared for weaving. Verify the edition behind the inherited rendering; no new meaning is inferred.
Confirm the source-number equivalence of prs225/5 and PrS77/23 before updating citation metadata.
Nonhuman subjects include tale animals and creatures weaving on water; the latter are called zaqore, but their species is uncertain
